name: Yüan Chēn
bio: Yüan Chēn (AD 779–831) was the close friend of the poet Po Chü-i. He is also the author of the prose tale “The Story of Ts’ui Ying-ying,” which is not included here. Waley’s translation of his dream-poem “The Pitcher” appears in More Translations from the Chinese.
The poems here are Arthur Waley’s version in More Translations from the Chinese (1919), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: At an Old Palace
poems.author: Yüan Chēn
poems.text:
Deserted now the Imperial bowers
Save by some few poor lonely flowers
One white-haired dame,
An Emperor's flame,
Sits down and tells of bygone hours.
